company_notes: Summary: evaluating Redwood Dedicated for low-latency trading assistant + reranking — main concern is alignment on latency SLO definitions and how we measure them (client vs server).
Ask from Summit: clear, auditable SLOs for p50/p95/p99; separate metric buckets for streaming (token-by-token/first-byte) and non-streaming (full-response); agreement on measurement endpoints.

Proposed targets (internal): non-streaming p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 < 250ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens); streaming first-byte p50 < 30ms, p95 < 90ms, p99 < 180ms — Summit is flexible but wants guarantees for trading use-case.
Important: Summit measures end-to-end (client-side) latency currently — wants Redwood to provide server-side breakdown and an agreed conversion method (client = server + network + client-render).

Measurement alignment items: sample period, synthetic load vs production telemetry, histogram retention (90d), and definition of cold/hot KV-cache warmup excluded from SLO for first 10 minutes after deploy or scale event.
Streaming vs non-streaming clarifications: streaming SLOs should capture time-to-first-token and token-emission-rate tail behavior; non-streaming SLOs measure total time to final chunk availability.

POC ask: 2-week perf run on Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) with Summit traffic replay to validate p95/p99 and throughput. Target throughput for POC: 350–450 rps with 99th percentile latency within negotiated SLOs.
Model profile: planning to serve a quantized Llama-3-13B variant + a smaller fallback (7B) for overload; require routing/fallback policy and deterministic latency profiles per model variant.
Operational requirements: N+1 capacity clause for burst windows, scheduled maintenance windows (max 4h/month), transparent incident timeline and credits formula in SLA.
Quote from CPO: "We will not accept black-box latency numbers — we need per-token and end-to-end traces to be able to correlate trading latency spikes."

Pricing sensitivity: will consider Dedicated commitment if unit economics for p95/p99 tails are predictable; interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations to lower per-token cost while keeping tail latency.

technical_requirements_summary: Throughput target: 350-450 RPS sustained for 2-hour windows; peak burst handling to 1.5x sustained for 10m without SLA penalty.
Latency SLOs to negotiate: non-streaming (total response) p50/p95/p99 targets; streaming to have both time-to-first-token and token-emission-tail targets.

Measurement definitions requested by Summit: client-side end-to-end, server-side request-accept to last-byte, network latency separately instrumented; agreement to use server-side telemetry as single source-of-truth for SLA credits.
Reserved GPU planning: prefer 8x A100-class equivalents (or AMD equivalent) with predictable allocation, support for continuous batching and KV cache persistence across warms.
Fallback strategy: automatic model downgrade (13B -> 7B) on capacity constraints with deterministic routing policy and explicit latency delta guarantees for fallback path.
Observability: per-request traces, token-level timing, histogram exports (Prometheus + s3 snapshots), 90-day telemetry retention for compliance audits.
SLA ask: 99.9% uptime target, credit formula tied to p99 miss-rate and availability; procurement wants explicit maintenance windows and RTO/RPO clauses.
Test harness: Summit will provide anonymized replay; Redwood to run both synthetic microbenchmarks and production-replay to show tail behavior under real patterns.
